label: 0 input at step 3-5 of an f-initial sequence after q/c/v/w
explanation: Very sparse conjunctive feature (175 dev steps). Almost all activity (98% of mass) is in the original phase at steps 3-5 (step 4 alone holds 74%), and 93% of mass is in sequences whose first token is f. Inside that window it fires most often and most strongly when the input is the digit 0 (69% of mass), and when earlier inputs include q, c, v or w, especially q right before the current step (e.g. f v c q [0] is the max). This reads like an additive combination of these cues and not a clean rule: the full conjunction has precision ~0.5 but recall only ~0.2 (dev mass recall 0.42), and the broad window predicate (f first, step 3-5) reaches 0.90 mass recall at near-zero precision. Weak activations also show up on non-0 inputs (letters o, b, t, d) after f..q prefixes, and a few times at the delimiter. I did not test magnitude beyond the top examples, which mostly have f first, q at step 3 and 0 at step 4. It never fires in the copy phase or at steps 0-2 or 6 and later, and almost never on sequences that do not start with f.
